strategy.summary: Build pandas at the buggy commit e49e355cad46 from source (Cython extension, editable install), then run the single parametrized test test_construction_from_min_timestamp. On the buggy revision the ms parameter should raise the PD_CHECK_OVERFLOW overflow error when constructing Period from Timestamp.min.value at millisecond resolution, so the test fails. On the fixed revision (PR 63609) the scale_time_with_underflow_check split avoids negative overflow and all three ms/us/ns parameters pass. The transition is the success criterion. The evidence does not state the Python version or any dependency pins, so those are chosen here and flagged in risks.

system_packages: a C compiler (gcc or clang) with a C++ toolchain
pinned_because: No version pin for NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata or Cython is documented or era-inferred (all kind unbounded); the unpinned choice here is the latest versions compatible with the buggy commit's build, and this is a choice, not an evidence-backed constraint
Python version is not stated by the evidence; plan assumes a CPython 3.x version supported by the buggy commit's pyproject.toml, to be confirmed from that file

strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision e49e355cad46 the freq='ms' case fails because Period(ts, freq='ms') raises the PD_CHECK_OVERFLOW overflow error for ts = Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit='ms'); on the fixed PR 63609 revision all three parametrized cases (ms, us, ns) complete without exception and the test passes.
strategy.numerical_probe: Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit='ms') followed by Period(ts, freq='ms') should not raise; the exact expected Period integer is not stated in the evidence and is not needed for the transition.

input_output_examples.input: Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit='ms') then Period(ts, freq='ms') (test_construction_from_min_timestamp, GH-63278)
input_output_examples.expected_output: successful conversion with no exception; exact Period value not stated in the evidence

risks: Stale compiled extension: the fix lives in compiled Cython/C code, so the fixed revision must be rebuilt (rerun the editable install) or the test will keep failing for the wrong reason; likewise the buggy build must be rebuilt after checkout.

Failure mode must be the intended one: on the buggy revision check that the error is the PD_CHECK_OVERFLOW overflow in the ms path, not an OutOfBoundsDatetime raised earlier inside Timestamp(...) construction, which would be a different failure than the one the fix addresses.
Only the ms parameter is expected to flip; us and ns may already pass on the buggy revision, so the transition is decided by the ms case alone.

The evidence does not state the platform; the overflow is pure int64 arithmetic and should be platform-independent, but if the defect was observed only under a specific architecture or compiler flag the transition may not reproduce elsewhere.

Dependency versions (NumPy, Cython, python-dateutil, tzdata) are unbounded in the evidence; a NumPy 2.x vs 1.x mismatch could change Timestamp construction behaviour and must be checked if the ms case does not fail on the buggy build.
Python version and any Cython or meson-python pins are not documented; if the editable build fails, pin Cython and meson-python to versions the buggy pyproject.toml allows.
The test runs three parameters under -k; to isolate the ms transition use -k 'test_construction_from_min_timestamp and ms'.

oracle.why: Conversion is exact integer scaling; the test asserts absence of overflow exception rather than a numeric tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On e49e355cad46 Period(Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit='ms'), freq='ms') goes through scaleSecondsToMilliseconds with no underflow split, so the negative multiplication overflows int64 and PD_CHECK_OVERFLOW raises, failing the ms parameter of the test.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On PR 63609 the ms path calls scale_time_with_underflow_check, computing a*(x+k)+(b-a*k) so no negative overflow occurs; the conversion succeeds and the ms, us and ns cases all pass.
